This is fundamentally different from the current incremental add/swap approach — it directly optimizes the conflict graph.

The key insight: the "bad triple" condition defines a 3-uniform hypergraph. We can convert this to a graph problem by noting that if we fix the order in which elements are considered, we can use a branch-and-bound approach where the state is just the current set (as a bitmask) and we check conflicts incrementally. With N=128, a 128-bit integer bitmask makes membership and iteration very fast.
